chunks: My father narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Mahziyar, from his father, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from Fudalah ibn Ayyub, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: The one who killed al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was a child of fornication, and the one who killed Yahya ibn Zakariyya (peace be upon him) was a child of fornication. And indeed, it was said: The sky turned red when al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was killed, for a year. Then he said: The sky and the earth wept over al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) and over Yahya ibn Zakariyya (peace be upon him), and its redness is its weeping.

key_terms.احْمَرَّتِ السَّمَاءُ: The sky turned red (cosmic sign of grief)

ai.seo_question: What are the cosmic signs of grief mentioned in Shia tradition regarding the martyrdom of Imam al-Husayn?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) highlights the divine pattern of martyrdom by noting that both the killer of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) and Yahya ibn Zakariyya (a.s.) were illegitimate, underscoring a spiritual lineage of conflict. The narration further describes the cosmic grief of creation, where the sky’s redness for a year symbolizes the weeping of the heavens and earth, a motif deeply rooted in Shia eschatology and tafsir.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 21. My father narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan (ibn ‘Ali) ibn Mahziyār, from his father, from ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from Ḥasan ibn Sa’īd, from Faďālah ibn Ayyūb, from Dāwūd ibn Farqad, who said:

I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) say: The killer of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.) was conceived illegitimately and the killer of Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā (a.s.) was (also) conceived illegitimately. When Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.) was killed, the heavens turned red for one year. The heavens and the earth have (only) wept over Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.) and Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā (a.s.), and the heavens weep by becoming red.
